title: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes
seo_title: Biotechnology Class 12 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 9)
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 9 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes: restriction enzymes, vectors, selectable markers, gel electrophoresis, PCR, transformation, bioreactors and downstream processing. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Cut with a restriction enzyme, join with DNA ligase, carry with a vector.
key_sub: PCR: denaturation → annealing → extension; DNA doubles each cycle.
body_html:
How to think about it

Recombinant DNA technology cuts DNA with restriction enzymes (such as EcoRI, which cuts at GAATTC and leaves sticky ends), joins it into a vector with DNA ligase and puts it into a competent host. A good vector has an origin of replication, selectable markers such as antibiotic resistance, and a cloning site; insertional inactivation of lacZ gives white recombinant colonies.

Fragments are separated by gel electrophoresis (smaller ones move further towards the anode) and seen with ethidium bromide. PCR copies DNA in cycles of denaturation, primer annealing and extension by heat-stable Taq polymerase, doubling it each cycle. Products are made in bioreactors and purified by downstream processing.

Example

2 molecules after 5 PCR cycles?

2 × 2⁵

Answer: 64

Example

Enzyme that joins DNA?

seals the backbone

Answer: DNA ligase

Common mistakes

  • Saying DNA moves to the cathode.
  • Forgetting that DNA doubles in every PCR cycle.
  • Thinking blue colonies are recombinant.

faq.a: It comes from a hot-spring bacterium and is not destroyed at the high temperature used to separate the DNA strands.
